chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: Chicago's South Side and meeting Al Hibbler
summary: After hours the musicians go to the South Side's Rhumboogie and Regal Theatre, where he befriends singer Al Hibbler.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Then, the fact is that Chicago at that particular time, like all other cities, had its sections where the Blacks lived and congregated. Now, this was all downtown in what they call the Loop in Chicago. But afterwards, everybody went out to the South Side, White and Black, and that's when they had clubs out there like the... They had a club called the Rhumboogie where Coleman Hawkins was playing. There was a club where Joe Williams used to work, one of the most popular... I can't remember now. I'll think of it after a while. [ED: CLUB DE LISA] There was a theatre, the Regal Theatre, where there was always somebody playing. And they had so many little places on the South Side where musicians were playing. In the hotels where we lived there were musicians playing.

This is actually where I really met my very good and lifetime friend, Al Hibbler, the singer. Since then we've had many associations. I really met him out there, and he and I became very fast friends. It was just an enjoyable time.
